correctness.rationale: Coalition maximum matching equals min(i,j) plus one when the marked pair is present and enough A-side members remain, giving the stated grand worth. Edge-pair coalitions characterize the core and the positive fractional edge matching gives a sharp dual first-ratio bound in the core-empty a=b+1 regime. In each core-bearing regime, explicit proper coalition upper constraints and relative-interior surplus quantization uniquely optimize the first variable lexicographic level, yielding exactly the five payoff regimes and core emptiness boundary. A separate direct exact-rational enumeration tested 35 parameter pairs and 11196 positive-valued proper-coalition ratios (including small matching examples); universality rests on the case proof, not these finite checks.
residual_risks: The finite check is corroborative only; all-parameter lexicographic optimality must follow from the explicit core and first nonfixed-stage arguments.

value.rationale: A complete bipartite matching market with one intra-side edge is a natural smallest non-bipartite deformation, exposing a sharp unique core failure when the side-size difference is one. The exact nucleon allocation changes in five structural regimes and provides a concrete comparison with generic multiplicative nucleon algorithms. Such complete all-parameter classifications are independently useful to cooperative game theory, beyond mere numerical instances or proof of computability.
residual_risks: The result is restricted to unweighted complete crossing edges and a single extra same-side edge.
